info.name: Consiva - DSR Fulfillment (Agent 3)
info.description:
API contract for the DSR Fulfillment agent, covering all 25 endpoints defined in backend/app/api/v1/routes/dsr.py (requests CRUD, classify, identity challenge/verify, search, results, evidence push/purge, execution-report, plan, action decision, execute, executions, response, complete, config/sources, config/retention x3, audit). Built ENTIRELY from static code reading -- the route handlers themselves, app/agents/dsr/services/*.py, app/agents/dsr/schemas/{case,evidence_push}.py, app/agents/dsr/errors.py, app/core/integration_auth.py, and app/main.py's exception handlers. NOT EXECUTED LIVE against any server: the only running stack on this box is production (docker-compose.prod.yml), which is strictly off-limits, so no request in this collection has been fired. To actually run it: point baseUrl at a non-production test deployment, obtain a real bearer token (a signed-in user's JWT from POST /api/v1/auth/login -- there is no separate DSR key), and replace every placeholder id variable with a real one from that environment, in the order the folders run (most later folders depend on state created by earlier ones in the SAME case).

Auth: the signed-in user's bearer JWT (app/core/security.get_current_user); the configuration writes additionally require the administrator role. There is no DSR key. The org comes from the verified token; nothing accepts an org_id from the caller.

Error envelope: DSR is NOT under the `/api/v1/consent-agent` prefix, so it gets the plain `{"detail": ...}` envelope (app/main.py consiva_error_handler / validation_error_handler, default branch), same as Purpose Classifier -- for a ConsivaError subclass, `detail` is a string; for a FastAPI RequestValidationError, `detail` is the default list of {loc, msg, type} objects.

Non-disclosure: every route keyed by {request_id} resolves it through case_service.get_case_or_raise, which treats a case in another org exactly like one that does not exist -> 404 for both, never 403/403-like disclosure (§37). The same pattern applies to {rule_id} and {action_id}.

Findings surfaced while building this collection (full detail in the agent's task report): (1) POST /requests/{id}/response creates a new row every call but returns 200, while POST /requests/{id}/evidence (also row-creating) returns 201 -- an inconsistency within this same file (folder 17). (2) GET /requests?limit=N silently clamps >200 rather than 422ing, unlike every other limit param in this codebase (folder 2). (3) _require_admin's role check returns 409 (CaseNotReadyError) for what is really an authorization failure, where 403 is used for the equivalent case everywhere else in this same file (folders 21/23/24). (4) Two AUDIT_* constants in schemas/case.py (AUDIT_IDENTITY_FAILED, AUDIT_RESULTS_FOUND) are defined but never actually recorded anywhere -- a failed identity-verification attempt leaves no audit trail at all (folder 6).

item.name: Domain error - wrong code (never raises; reports unsatisfied)

request.description: MUTATES STATE (increments verification.attempts) but returns 200, not an error: identity_service.submit_challenge's docstring is explicit that it 'never raises on a wrong answer' so that 'wrong code' and 'no such verification in progress' are not distinguishable from outside -- a deliberate anti-enumeration design, same spirit as the 404 non-disclosure pattern elsewhere. NOTE (audit-trail gap, reported but not fixed -- outside this agent's editable route): neither this wrong-answer path nor the max-attempts-exhausted path writes ANY audit_service.record call, even though case.AUDIT_IDENTITY_FAILED ('dsr.identity_failed') exists in schemas/case.py and is never referenced anywhere in the codebase -- a failed identity check leaves no trace in the case's audit timeline at all.
